title: How early should you arrive at Belfast International Airport?
author: Brogan
cover_image_alt: A long, quiet airport terminal concourse at night with a clock and rows of seats
intro: About two hours before your flight is the usual advice for Belfast International, with a little more on early mornings and around Christmas and the summer holidays. Here's how to work out your timing, plus drop-off and getting there.
seo_description: About 2 hours before most flights, more on early mornings and peak dates. Belfast International security, liquids, the £5 drop-off and the Airport Express.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Hand luggage only:** about 2 hours
- **Bags to drop:** 2 to 2½ hours
- **Early mornings:** add 30 minutes
- **Christmas and summer:** add 30 minutes

This is the timing most airlines and travel guides suggest for Belfast International, checked in October 2026. Your airline's bag drop and gate deadlines are the ones that count, and they're on your booking. Procedures change, so check the airport's and the airline's current advice before you travel.

sections.heading: Belfast International or Belfast City?
sections.text:
Belfast has two airports, and it's easy to mix them up. Belfast International (code BFS) is the big one, about 30 minutes north-west of the city near Antrim, and it's where easyJet, Jet2 and Ryanair fly from. George Best Belfast City (code BHD) is the smaller one right by the city centre, used mainly by Aer Lingus Regional, British Airways and Loganair.

Watch out: check which one is on your booking before you set off. They're about 40 minutes apart by road, and turning up at the wrong one is a mistake you can't fix in a hurry.

Belfast International has a single terminal, so once you're at the right airport there's no terminal to choose.

sections.heading: Security, liquids and busy times
sections.text:
The airport opened a new security hall with modern scanners, so you can usually leave your liquids and electronics in your hand luggage. The size limit hasn't gone, though: according to the airport, liquids still need to be in containers of 100ml or less.

Security is usually quick outside the peaks. The busy times are the early morning wave of departures, when many holiday flights leave at once, and the run-up to Christmas, when the airport has reported record passenger numbers. The summer holidays and the July holidays in Northern Ireland are busy too.

| Trip | Flight | Arrive |
| --- | --- | --- |
| City break, hand luggage only | Midday, midweek | **About 2 hours** before |
| Sun holiday, bags to drop | 6am in July | **2½ hours** before |
| Christmas trip, bags to drop | Mid-December weekend | **2½ hours** before |

sections.heading: Bag drop and the gate
sections.image_alt: A row of empty airport check-in desks with queue barriers in front
sections.image_caption: Bag drop closes well before your flight, so work back from that deadline.
sections.text:
If you're checking a bag, plan around the bag drop deadline, not the departure time. Budget airlines usually close bag drop 40 to 60 minutes before departure, and they don't make exceptions. The exact time is in your booking.

The gate closes before the published departure time too, often about 30 minutes before.

Tip: check in online as soon as it opens, and if you're travelling with hand luggage only, keep your boarding pass on your phone and go straight to security.

sections.heading: Getting there and dropping off
sections.text:
- **By bus:** the Airport Express 300 runs between Belfast city centre and the airport, and is the easiest way without a car. Early services are less frequent, so check the timetable for the hour you need.
- **Drop-off:** the drop-off zone beside the terminal costs £5 for up to 10 minutes since March 2026. There's also a free drop-off area in the long stay car park, a short walk away.
- **Parking:** booking ahead is much cheaper than turning up.
- **By car:** allow extra time on the M2 at rush hour.

If you're coming from further afield, such as Derry, Coleraine or the border counties, allow plenty of time for the drive on winter mornings.

sections.heading: Five ways to make the airport easier
sections.text:
- **Check the airport name** on your booking: International, not City.
- **Travel with hand luggage only** if you can.
- **Pack liquids to 100ml**, so you're fine at both ends of the trip.
- **Work back from your bag drop deadline**, not the departure time.
- **Allow more time in December**, when the airport is at its busiest.

sections.heading: Where could you go from Belfast International?
sections.text:
easyJet has its biggest Northern Ireland base here, with flights to cities, the Canaries and, this winter, new routes to [Rome](/destinations/rome) and Sharm El Sheikh. For winter sun, look at [Lanzarote](/destinations/lanzarote) or [Tenerife](/destinations/tenerife), and for a city break, [Krakow](/destinations/krakow) or [Barcelona](/destinations/barcelona).

The [city breaks](/destinations/city-breaks) and [Christmas holidays](/destinations/christmas-holidays) pages have more ideas. If your family can't agree, read our guide to [deciding where to go on holiday](/how-to-decide-where-to-go-on-holiday), or put everyone's picks into a draw.

faqs.question: How early should I get to Belfast International Airport?
faqs.answer: About two hours before a flight with hand luggage only, and two to two and a half hours if you have a bag to drop. Allow more on early mornings and around Christmas.

faqs.question: Is Belfast International the same as Belfast City Airport?
faqs.answer: No. Belfast International (BFS) is near Antrim, about 30 minutes from the city. George Best Belfast City (BHD) is next to the city centre. Check which one is on your booking.

faqs.question: How much is drop-off at Belfast International Airport?
faqs.answer: Since March 2026, the drop-off zone beside the terminal costs £5 for up to 10 minutes. There's a free drop-off area in the long stay car park.

faqs.question: Can you take liquids through security at Belfast International?
faqs.answer: Yes, in containers of up to 100ml. The new scanners mean you can usually leave them in your bag.
